steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Audience theories attempt to explain the relationship between media products and audiences — how media affects people and how people use media. | Key Fact: Hypodermic needle model (1920s-1930s): media injects ideas directly into passive audiences, who are uniformly affected. Now largely discredited but still influences public concern about media effects. | Key Fact: Two-step flow model (Katz and Lazarsfeld, 1955): media messages pass through opinion leaders (influential people) who interpret and pass them on to wider audiences. More nuanced than the hypodermic model. | Key Fact: Uses and Gratifications theory (Blumler and Katz, 1974): audiences actively choose media to fulfil four needs — information/education, entertainment, social interaction, and personal identity.
